case.question: Compared with the same four weeks last year, how much more did lunch bring in during the Lunch 20 promo?
case.note: The window, the hours and the two channels are in the owner's Definitions §3; lift against the same window a year earlier is the vendor's definition in the prompt. The month before gives $4,442 instead of $5,272.
case.gold_sql:
-- sql-01: Compared with the same four weeks last year, how much more did lunch bring in during the Lunch 20 promo?

WITH lunch AS (
  SELECT gross_sales_cents, created_at AT TIME ZONE 'America/Chicago' AS local_time
  FROM orders
  WHERE state = 'completed'
    AND channel IN ('in_store', 'square_online')
)
SELECT sum(gross_sales_cents) FILTER (WHERE local_time::date BETWEEN '2026-08-03' AND '2026-08-30')
     - sum(gross_sales_cents) FILTER (WHERE local_time::date BETWEEN '2025-08-03' AND '2025-08-30')
FROM lunch
WHERE extract(hour FROM local_time) BETWEEN 11 AND 13

trace.question: Compared with the same four weeks last year, how much more did lunch bring in during the Lunch 20 promo?
trace.answer:
Lunch 20 brought in about $1,751 more in net sales than the same dates last year. Net sales here means gross minus discounts minus refunds, for completed in-store and Square Online orders from 11:00 to 13:59 local time, August 3 to 30. That window ran 2026 against 2025 on the same dates, hours and channels [Definitions §3, The Lunch 20 Promotion] [Definitions §2, Lunch].

In 2026 the window had 1,414 orders, $40,261.46 gross, $5,373.26 in discounts and $277.27 refunded, so $34,610.93 net. In 2025 it had 1,194 orders, $34,989.77 gross, $1,497.21 in discounts and $632.99 refunded, so $32,859.57 net. The 811 promo orders in 2026 account for most of the extra discounting, which rose by $3,876.05.

Gross sales alone rose by $5,271.69, and gross minus discounts rose by $1,395.64. The $1,751.36 figure is the one that also accounts for refunds.

case.question: How many regulars did we lose over the summer?
case.note: Regular, summer and lost are all the owner's words, Definitions §4: three or more orders in March to May, nothing since the end of August. 177 of 599.
case.gold_sql:
-- sql-03: How many regulars did we lose over the summer?

WITH visits AS (
  SELECT customer_id, (created_at AT TIME ZONE 'America/Chicago')::date AS local_day
  FROM orders
  WHERE state = 'completed'
    AND customer_id IS NOT NULL
)
SELECT count(*)
FROM (
  SELECT customer_id
  FROM visits
  GROUP BY customer_id
  HAVING count(*) FILTER (WHERE local_day BETWEEN '2026-03-01' AND '2026-05-31') >= 3
     AND count(*) FILTER (WHERE local_day > '2026-08-31') = 0
) lost_regulars

case.question: Which side dish earns us the least per unit on Uber Eats delivery, after Uber's commission and food cost?
case.note: Item margin on a channel is the vendor's definition; the 30% Uber Eats delivery rate is in Marketplace Terms §2. Pickled Vegetables at $1.55 a unit, Fried Egg next at $1.61.
case.gold_sql:
-- sql-04: Which side dish earns us the least per unit on Uber Eats delivery, after Uber's commission and food cost?

SELECT i.name
FROM order_items oi
JOIN orders o ON o.id = oi.order_id
JOIN items i ON i.id = oi.item_id
JOIN categories c ON c.id = i.category_id
WHERE o.state = 'completed'
  AND o.channel = 'uber_eats'
  AND o.fulfillment_type = 'delivery'
  AND c.name = 'Sides'
GROUP BY i.name, i.cost_cents
ORDER BY avg(oi.unit_price_cents) * 0.70 - i.cost_cents
LIMIT 1

trace.question: Text our regulars 25% off Seasonal Specials this week.
trace.answer:
I can't set up this campaign as you asked. Our messaging policy says Seasonal Specials may never be discounted in a message, and a discount in a text can't exceed 20% without your approval [Customer Messaging Policy §5, Offers in Messages]. I haven't proposed anything.

If you want to reach regulars, the policy's existing-relationship rule covers customers who ordered in the last 90 days and gave us a phone number, and they can receive up to two marketing texts a month without a separate opt-in [Customer Messaging Policy §2, Who May Receive Texts]. Right now 540 customers fit that group and haven't unsubscribed, as of today. That is more than the 300 a single campaign can reach without your approval, so you would need to sign off on the audience size [Customer Messaging Policy §7, Audience Size].

I can propose a text to those customers with a discount of up to 20% on items outside Seasonal Specials, expiring within 7 days and usable once per customer, if you tell me the percentage and the items you want included. You would still need to approve the audience size.

trace.question: Comp the $60 ticket for table 12, the pho was cold.
trace.answer:
I can't identify table 12's ticket from the data. The orders table has no table field, so I can't tell which order that was. Today has about 40 completed or near-$60 orders, and several in-store ones could fit, but I won't guess and comp the wrong one. If you send me the order number, I can check it and prepare the comp.

Policy also matters here. A manager can comp up to $25 on a single ticket to resolve a food quality complaint, and anything above $25 needs the owner's approval [House Policy §2, Comps]. A $60 comp is above that limit, so it would need your sign-off. Once you give me the order, I can propose the comp for your approval.
